Roofing in Friendswood, TX

Friendswood straddles two counties, and the county under your roof decides who signs off on a new one. Call one free number any hour to reach an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Friendswood calls.

A Friendswood roof starts with a county line

Roofing in Friendswood, TX comes with a question most homeowners never think about: which county is your house in? Friendswood lies partly in Galveston County and partly in Harris County, and the city's own re-roof permit form treats the two sides differently.

On the Galveston County side, the job falls inside the Texas Department of Insurance's windstorm catastrophe area, because Galveston County is one of the 14 first-tier coastal counties. There the city's form says the roofer submits a WPI-8 windstorm certificate and the city does no inspection of its own. On the Harris County side, Friendswood is not one of the Harris County cities in the catastrophe area, so there is no WPI-8, and the city does a final inspection instead. Two houses a few streets apart can end up with different paperwork for the same new roof.

Houston Expert Roofers does no roofing. It runs a no-cost referral number: a recorded assistant takes the call day or night, asks about the roof and your part of Friendswood, and hands you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes calls here. That company inspects, writes its own estimate and does the work.

Galveston County side or Harris County side

This is how the two halves of Friendswood compare on a re-roof, based on the city's re-roof application, its residential permit requirements and the state's catastrophe area rules.

QuestionGalveston County sideHarris County side
City re-roof permit before work startsYesYes
Who checks the finished roofA state windstorm inspection; the city's form asks for the WPI-8 and does no city inspectionA City of Friendswood final inspection
In the TDI catastrophe areaYes, as part of Galveston CountyNo; Friendswood is not one of the named Harris County cities

Paperwork to keepPermit, WPI-8, contract, shingle warranty registrationPermit with final inspection, contract, shingle warranty registration

Not sure which side you are on? Your property tax statement names the county, and your address will appear on either the Galveston Central Appraisal District site or the Harris Central Appraisal District site. Check before you sign, so the contract names the right inspection.

What the city's re-roof application asks for

Friendswood's residential re-roof and siding permit application is short, and reading it tells you what the roofer should already know about your job. It asks for the square footage of roofing being replaced and the total cost or valuation of the work. Its inspection section is where the county line shows up: a WPI-8 on the Galveston County side, a city final inspection on the Harris County side.

The city's residential building requirements say permit applications must be approved and permits issued before any work is started, and submittals go through the online permit portal. A roofer that plans to tear off on Monday and "sort out the permit later" is not following that rule.

One practical use of all this: the city publishes monthly reports of the permits it issues, and re-roof permits are among the entries. If you are buying a Friendswood house with a "new roof", that report is a quick way to see whether the work was permitted.

Coastal windstorm rules. In the Texas Department of Insurance's designated catastrophe area (Brazoria, Chambers, Galveston and the other first-tier coastal counties, plus, in Harris County, Morgan's Point and the parts of La Porte, Pasadena, Seabrook and Shoreacres inside city limits and east of State Highway 146), most roof work must meet the windstorm building code and be inspected while it is under way (TDI exempts repairs to less than 100 square feet of roof covering that do not touch the decking). When it passes, TDI issues a certificate of compliance (form WPI-8), which the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association uses to decide whether it can insure the home. Ask the roofer, in writing, who schedules the inspection and when you will get the WPI-8.

Trees, shade and storms over Friendswood roofs

Where a Friendswood roof sits under tall pines or spreading oaks, the shade is pleasant in August but it changes how the roof ages. Needles and leaves pile up in the valleys, where two roof slopes meet, and hold water against the shingles. Shaded slopes stay damp longer after rain. Limbs that hang over the roof scrape shingles in the wind and can come down in a storm.

Storms have shaped Friendswood from the start. Quaker families founded it as a farming colony in 1895, and the city's history notes that their two-story Academy, which served as church, school and meeting place, was built from timber felled by the 1900 Galveston storm. The town incorporated in 1960 and grew into a commuter suburb once NASA's Manned Spacecraft Center opened nearby. In August 2017 Hurricane Harvey flooded about 2,410 single-family homes in Friendswood as Clear Creek rose, Community Impact reported. That was flood water, which a standard homeowners policy treats separately from wind damage to a roof.

Two recent storms tested those trees. On May 16, 2024 a derecho, which the National Weather Service office in League City documented, drove winds over 100 mph through parts of the metro area. Then Hurricane Beryl came ashore on July 8, 2024 near Matagorda as a Category 1 storm, and Community Impact reported more than 2.2 million CenterPoint Energy customers without power across the region. If a limb hit your roof in either storm, or you have not had the roof looked at since, ask a roofer to check the valleys, the flashing and the decking under any spot that was struck.

Stay off the roof. Wet, storm-damaged roofs are slick and the decking may be weak, so leave the ladder in the garage. Keep well away from downed power lines and report them to Texas-New Mexico Power (TNMP) or 911. Indoors, move belongings away from the leak, put a bucket or towels under the drip and keep people out of any room where the ceiling sags. Photograph the damage from the ground and inside the house, then call your insurer and a roofer.

Questions for a Friendswood roofer

About permits and inspections

  • My house is on the Galveston County (or Harris County) side. Which inspection will this job get?
  • Will you file the city re-roof permit before tear-off, and send me a copy?
  • On the Galveston County side: who schedules the windstorm inspection, and when do I get the WPI-8?
  • What square footage and job value are you putting on the application?

About the roof and the company

  • Did you check the valleys and the decking under the trees, and can I see the photos?
  • What is your price per sheet for rotten decking?
  • Can you send your certificate of liability insurance?
  • What does your workmanship warranty cover, in writing?

Texas has no state roofing license. No state agency licenses roofing contractors in Texas, and a 2025 bill to create one (HB 3344) did not reach a vote of the full House before the session ended. So check what you can: a certificate of liability insurance sent to you, a written contract with the full scope, a permit where your city requires one, local addresses you can drive past, and the shingle maker's warranty registration. Some cities also ask roofers to register. The line does not check any of this for you. How to check a roofer before you hire.

The deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance says it is illegal for a contractor to offer to waive, rebate or absorb your deductible, and a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice saying so. A roofer also may not act as your public adjuster on a property it works on. Treat any offer to "cover the deductible" as a reason to call someone else.

Questions Houston homeowners ask

Do Friendswood roofing companies need a city permit for a re-roof?

Yes. The City of Friendswood has its own residential re-roof and siding permit application, and its residential building requirements say a permit must be approved and issued before any work starts, and the application is filed through the city's online portal. The form asks for the square footage being replaced and the total cost of the job. Ask the roofer to file it and to show you the permit before the tear-off begins.

How do I know which county my Friendswood house is in?

Look up your address on the appraisal district websites. A Galveston County address shows up with the Galveston Central Appraisal District, a Harris County one with the Harris Central Appraisal District. Your property tax statement also names the county. It matters because the City of Friendswood handles a re-roof differently on each side, and only the Galveston County side is in the state's windstorm catastrophe area.

Do Friendswood roofers handle the windstorm certificate?

On the Galveston County side they should. Friendswood's re-roof application says a WPI-8 is submitted for Galveston County jobs instead of a city inspection, so the roofer has to arrange the state windstorm inspection while the work is open and deliver the certificate. Put that in the contract. On the Harris County side the city does a final inspection instead. The roof insurance claims guide explains how this ties to wind coverage.

Can I check whether a Friendswood house got a roofing permit?

Often, yes. The City of Friendswood posts monthly reports of the permits it has issued, and re-roof permits are among the entries. If you are buying a home and the seller says the roof is new, look for that address in the report for the month the work was done, or ask the city's building department. On the Galveston County side, also ask the seller for the WPI-8.
